name: Yet Another Counting Problem
description: You are given two integers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, and $$$q$$$ queries. The $$$i$$$-th query consists of two numbers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$, and the answer to it is the number of integers $$$x$$$ such that $$$l_i \le x \le r_i$$$, and $$$((x \bmod a) \bmod b) \ne ((x \bmod b) \bmod a)$$$. Calculate the answer for each query. Recall that $$$y \bmod z$$$ is the remainder of the division of $$$y$$$ by $$$z$$$. For example, $$$5 \bmod 3 = 2$$$, $$$7 \bmod 8 = 7$$$, $$$9 \bmod 4 = 1$$$, $$$9 \bmod 9 = 0$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. Then the test cases follow. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le a, b \le 200$$$; $$$1 \le q \le 500$$$). Then $$$q$$$ lines follow, each containing two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \le l_i \le r_i \le 10^{18}$$$) for the corresponding query.
output_specification: For each test case, print $$$q$$$ integers — the answers to the queries of this test case in the order they appear.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1342C — Yet Another Counting Problem [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
